answer: Threshold blind signature issuance lets a quorum sign a message they cannot see, and the spiral of the design is that the user blinds the message before sending it to any issuer. The trellis of the protocol is that each issuer's partial signature is verified before combination, so a faulty issuer is caught early. A Sybil cannot obtain extra signed tokens because issuance requires a threshold of independent issuers, and the vertex of the blinding protects the honest user's privacy.
